title: 1987 AMC 8 Problem 20
statement: Consider the statement: “If a whole number \(n\) is not prime, then the whole number \(n - 2\) is not prime.” Which of the following values of \(n\) shows this statement to be false?

solutions.text:
A counterexample needs \(n\) not prime but \(n - 2\) prime. For \(n = 9,\) the number \(9\) is not prime while \(9 - 2 = 7\) is prime, so it breaks the statement.

The others fail to be counterexamples: \(12 - 2 = 10\) and \(16 - 2 = 14\) are not prime, while \(13\) and \(23\) are themselves prime.

Thus, the correct answer is A .
hints: To disprove an “if ... then” statement, find a case where the “if” part holds but the “then” part fails
Look for \(n\) that is not prime while \(n - 2\) is prime
